inputs.xtext_rule_text:
fragment FeatureDeclaration returns SysML::Feature :
	( isSufficient ?= 'all' )? 
	( Identification ( FeatureSpecializationPart | FeatureConjugationPart )?
	| FeatureSpecializationPart
	| FeatureConjugationPart
	)
	FeatureRelationshipPart*
;

decision: An optional `all`, then an identification with an optional specialization or conjugation part, or one of those parts alone, then any number of relationship parts — as KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it. It cannot be empty: every alternative needs a name or a part.
notes:
THE CLAUSE IS FLAGGED MALFORMED AND THIS PRODUCTION IS NOT AFFECTED. The pack reports an unmatched `)` on line 8 of the Features clause. That line is inside the Feature production — its own parentheses close at -1 — and this production's parentheses balance on their own, so it is derived from the clause as written. The repair of Feature is recorded on the Feature unit.

THE XTEXT DIFFERS AND IS NOT FOLLOWED. The pilot writes `Identification` where the clause writes `FeatureIdentification`, and `FeatureConjugationPart` where it writes `ConjugationPart`. The first is not a rename. The pilot's Identification is `( '<' Name '>' )? Name?`, both parts optional, so its FeatureDeclaration can match nothing; the clause's FeatureIdentification requires a name. So where a declaration is mandatory — the second alternative of Feature, `EndFeaturePrefix FeatureDeclaration` — the pilot accepts a bare `end;` and the clause does not.

THE CORPUS DOES NOT DECIDE IT. No KerML file writes `end` with no declaration after it; the forms are `end feature ...` (70), `end [0..1]`, and `end cart:`, all of which both readings accept. The clause is normative and the corpus does not contradict it, so it is followed, and the difference is recorded rather than raised as a conflict — the same footing as the Import unit.

FOR A PARSER AUTHOR: after the optional `all`, a NAME or `<` starts the first alternative, and a specialization or conjugation token starts the other two.

evidence.note: states FeatureDeclaration with FeatureIdentification and ConjugationPart
